title: Effect of Hot Extrusion on a Li-modified A356 Al Alloy
content: A356 aluminum alloy, known for its high mechanical properties and excellent castability, is particularly relevant in various industrial applications, especially in the automotive and aerospace sectors [1]. Additionally, hot extrusion is one of the most cost-effective processing methods for producing high-strength aluminum alloys [2]. In this sense, hot extrusion has significantly improved ductility and strength [3]. The capability to modify the microstructure through hot extrusion and subsequent heat treatments allows manufacturers to customize the properties of A356 for specific applications, increasing its significance in modern engineering. Lithium is recognized for its ability to decrease the density of aluminum alloys, making it especially beneficial in aerospace applications where weight reduction is crucial [4]. Adding lithium can lower the melting point of aluminum alloys, enhancing their processability. For instance, it has been shown that the melting point of aluminum-lithium alloys can be significantly reduced compared to conventional aluminum alloys, which facilitates more effortless casting and processing [5]. Thus, adding Li to an A356 alloy can enhance the effects of hot extrusion on its properties.
